name: Uffizi
funding: State museum under the Ministry of Culture. Donors include Veronica Atkins (€4.5M, Boboli amphitheatre), Edwin L. Wiegand Foundation ($1M, Vasari Corridor), Ferragamo (€600k, 2014) and Fondazione CR Firenze.
watch: Contract workers protested before Botticelli's Venus on 5 April 2026 over outsourced jobs. Climate activists hit its paintings in 2022 and 2024; no funder targeted.
records_note: No annual report; its transparency portal posts accounts for 2023 to 2026 and a five-member board, and the donation page names donors, mostly undated.

name: Amon Carter Museum
funding: Founded by the Amon G. Carter Foundation, still a $100,000+ donor. FY2025: 1,387 donors gave $4.8M; public grants from Fort Worth, Arts Fort Worth, Texas Commission on the Arts.
watch: In October 2024 the museum closed its Cowboy show for two weeks and reopened it with a mature-content warning; artist rafa esparza called it censorship.
records_note: Annual reports 2018 to 2025 on its site carry a dated donor list, financial highlights and trustees; Form 990s are on ProPublica.

name: BALTIC Centre for Contemporary Art
funding: Opened July 2002 with £33.4M of Arts Council lottery capital; Gateshead Council backed the building. Corporate supporters include Tommee Tippee and NorthStandard.
watch: In March 2018 Baltic said it took no BAE money for the Great Exhibition of the North; BAE withdrew. Nissan appears only in photo captions.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; a supporters page names funders and patrons, undated; trustees are listed.

name: S.M.A.K.
funding: City of Ghent and Flanders. Current partners include the National Lottery, Belfius, Jan De Nul, Interparking, Christie's, Hiscox and Duvel. ENGIE has supported art workshops since 2012.
watch: Municipal contemporary museum of Ghent founded by Jan Hoet.
why_flagged: City of Ghent and Flanders. Current partners include the National Lottery, Belfius, Jan De Nul, Interparking, Christie's, Hiscox and Duvel. ENGIE has supported art workshops since 2012.
records_note: The museum posts no reports, accounts or board; its partners show as undated logos and a few names in text.

name: Art Gallery of Nova Scotia
funding: Provincial crown agency. 2024-25 supporters: Province, Arts Nova Scotia, Canada Council, BMO, Scotiabank, TD Bank Group, Ubisoft, the Sobey foundations and Benjamin Bridge winery.
watch: TD Bank pleaded guilty on 10 October 2024 to money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, paying about $3B.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2013-14 to 2025-26 and financial statements back to 2011-12; the 2024-25 report names supporters and the board page names directors.

name: Amos Rex
funding: Owned and run by the Amos Anderson Fund (formerly Konstsamfundet). Helsingin Sanomat is main partner; Genelec and Bauer Media Outdoor are partners.
watch: Privately funded non-profit museum established by the bequest of Amos Anderson. Konstsamfundet's endowment yields completely cover operating deficits, allowing total freedom from external corporate sponsorship or government subsidies.
records_note: Shows its main partner and partners as logos, names its owner the Amos Anderson Fund, and publishes no reports, accounts or board list.

name: Kiasma Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: €11M. Finnish Ministry of Education and Culture, Finnish National Gallery.
watch: State museum operating solely on national cultural funding; ethical gift policy.

name: Para Site
funding: Yenn and Alan Lo Foundation, Sunpride Foundation and Cheng-Lan Foundation lead the 2025 gala list. Galleries such as Gagosian, Zwirner and White Cube give; annual benefit auction and Patrons' Circle.
watch: Roster read via official website and public registry; gala sponsor logos are an image. No adverse finding.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; it names benefactors of its 2025 gala and an undated patrons' circle, and lists a nine-person board plus advisors.

name: M+ Museum
funding: HKD 380M operating budget, 2.5M annual visitors. West Kowloon Cultural District Authority (statutory body of the Hong Kong SAR Government).
watch: Monitored Governance: Major global museum of visual culture in West Kowloon designed by Herzog & de Meuron.

name: Contemporary Arts Museum Houston
funding: Warhol, Teiger, N2 Stone and Frank Liu Jr. foundations, NEA, City of Houston, Texas Commission on the Arts and Major Exhibition Fund donors, per 2026 credits. FY2025 expenses $6.1M.
watch: Non-collecting museum offering free admission to the public.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990s for 2011 to 2023 are on ProPublica, no standing donor list exists, and 20 trustees are named.

name: Henia Onstad Kunstsenter
funding: NOK 45M. Norwegian Ministry of Culture, Viken fylkeskommune, Bærum municipality.
watch: Public foundation with explicit fossil fuel sponsorship exclusion.

name: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
funding: 716k visitors in 2024. Kulturstyrelsen grant DKK 36.1M (about 26%); 2024 backers include Augustinus Fonden, A.P. Møller foundations, Ny Carlsbergfondet, Realdania, Novo Nordisk Fonden and Villum Fonden.
watch: Augustinus Fonden paid for many 2024 acquisitions and DKK 2M for the 2026 Freud show. Its investment arm holds over 25% of Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
why_flagged: 716k visitors in 2024. Kulturstyrelsen grant DKK 36.1M (about 26%); 2024 backers include Augustinus Fonden, A.P. Møller foundations, Ny Carlsbergfondet, Realdania, Novo Nordisk Fonden and Villum Fonden.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2008 to 2025 with audited accounts, names its six board members and lists 2024 sponsors and foundations.
